title: Weighted sum of a two-valued function
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set with real weights satisfying $\sum_iw_i=1$. Suppose $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ takes only the values $a$ and $b$, for some $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $\varphi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$. With $\gamma=\sum_{i:f_i=a}w_i$, one has
\[
\sum_iw_i\varphi(f_i)=\gamma\varphi(a)+(1-\gamma)\varphi(b).
\]
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, let real weights satisfy $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $f:I\to\bbr$ take values in $\{a,b\}$, where $a,b\in\bbr$. For any $\varphi:\bbr\to\bbr$, setting $\gamma=\sum_{i:f_i=a}w_i$ gives $\sum_iw_i\varphi(f_i)=\gamma\varphi(a)+(1-\gamma)\varphi(b)$.
